name: Screen-space Subdivision with Virtual Patches
definition: A rendering scheme where the screen is divided into small, separate 128x128-pixel patches in a virtual pixel space. Multiple independent SIMD engines (Renderers) operate on these disjoint patches simultaneously to achieve parallelism.
summary: Screen-space Subdivision with Virtual Patches is a parallel rendering scheme that divides the screen into small patches processed by independent SIMD engines, enabling flexible mapping and cost/performance trading.
